items.title: Email Campaign · : Referral Push (30-60 Day Post-Install Cohort)
items.preview:
**Why this one:** These 30 clients just spent thousands and are in the honeymoon window. They love their water right now. This is the single highest-intent moment to ask for a referral, and the cash structure gives a real reason to click. No hard rule conflicts (well past install, no service pitch, referral not review).
### 1. Campaign
- **Name:** New-Client Referral Window (30-60d)
- **Audience:** Referral push candidates, **30 members**
### 2. Subject line + alternates (60 char max)
- **Primary (specific):** `Your water's dialed in. Now there's $500 in it for you.`
- Alt 1 (curiosity): `The thing our happiest clients do around month one`
- Alt 2 (pain): `Your neighbor is still drinking that water`
- Alt 3 (authority): `How ClearWave grows (hint: it's you)`
- Alt 4 (specific): `$500, $750, $1,000: how referrals work here`
### 3. Preview text (90 char max)
`No review needed. Just one name. Here's exactly what you earn when they say yes.`
### 4. Email body
> Hi Anna,
>
> It's been about a month since we installed your Meridian, and by now the difference should be settling in: softer showers, cleaner glasses, water you actually want to drink.
>
> Here's the honest truth about how we grow. We don't chase. We let the water do the talking, and we ask the people who already trust us.
>
> So here's the ask. If you know someone fighting bad water, send them our way for a free water assessment. If they book a consult, you get a $50 gift card. If they become a client, you get real money:
>
> - $500 cash for each of your first five referrals this year
> - $750 for referrals six through nine
> - $1,000 each once you hit ten
>
> One name is all it takes to start. Just reply to this email with who comes to mind.
>
> Justin
> CEO / ClearWave
*(Merge tags: first name + system name. For "(not specified)" clients: "your ClearWave system." For legacy-name clients like Mina's Reionator: swap the product line for the tenure line, "It's been about a month since we installed your water system.")*
### 5. Send timing
**Tuesday, 10:00 AM ET**. Mid-morning, mid-week, avoids Monday inbox pileup and Friday drop-off.
### 6. Expected performance
- **Open: 46-50%** (above your 42.3% baseline; small warm cohort, personalized subject, recent buyers)
- **Click/reply: 4-8%** (dramatically above 0.28% baseline because the CTA is "reply with a name," not a link click, and there's real cash attached)
- **Conversion (referral names captured): 3-6 names**, with 1-2 likely to book. Even one closed referral pays for itself many times over.
### 7. Source justification
Draws from **Jobber lifecycle trigger: Referral push candidates (30-60 days post-install, satisfied)** and the **Referral Bonus Structure** (exact $500/$750/$1,000 tiers, $50 gift card). Honors Hard Rule 3 (referrals not reviews) and 3a ("free water assessment").
---

items.title: Email Campaign · : Concierge "Is It Worth It?" (13-24 Month Cohort)
items.preview:
**Why this one:** 100 clients, all past their year-1 service, so the hard 12-month floor is cleared. They've already experienced the service, so they trust it. The "here's the math" framing fits your low-pressure voice and this is a recurring-revenue play ($99/mo) with the largest eligible audience of the week.
### 1. Campaign
- **Name:** Concierge Year-1.5 Math
- **Audience:** Concierge upsell candidates, **100 members**
### 2. Subject line + alternates (60 char max)
- **Primary (curiosity):** `The question we get asked at 18 months`
- Alt 1 (specific): `Is Concierge worth it for you? Here's the math.`
- Alt 2 (pain): `Filter swaps, parts, service. Or one flat number.`
- Alt 3 (authority): `What we cover so you never think about it`
- Alt 4 (curiosity): `You've had your annual service. Now a fair question.`
### 3. Preview text (90 char max)
`No pressure, just the numbers. Whether Concierge makes sense depends on one thing.`
### 4. Email body
> Hi Jessica,
>
> It's been about a year and a half since we installed your water system, and you've now been through your first annual service. So this is the question we get asked most around this point: "Is this Concierge thing actually worth it for me?"
>
> Fair question. Here's the honest math.
>
> Concierge is $99/mo. For that you get:
>
> - Your annual service, handled
> - Filter swaps included
> - Priority phone support (you skip the line)
> - Parts coverage on your standard install components
>
> If you're the type who'd rather never think about filters, swaps, or a surprise parts bill, it's an easy yes. If you like handling things yourself and calling us only when you need us, staying pay-as-you-go is completely fine too. We're not here to push you either way.
>
> Want the real comparison for your exact setup? Reply "Concierge" and I'll have someone run your numbers.
>
> Justin
> CEO / ClearWave
*(Merge logic: all systems in this cohort are legacy names or non-current, so use the tenure line by default. If a current ClearWave name appears, it may be named.)*
### 5. Send timing
**Thursday, 11:00 AM ET**. Separated from Tuesday's referral send so the two campaigns don't overlap in the same inboxes (some clients could theoretically appear in future cohorts; spacing protects list health).
### 6. Expected performance
- **Open: 40-44%** (near baseline; larger, slightly older cohort, but curiosity subject and warm relationship hold it up)
- **Click/reply: 2-4%** (well above 0.28% because it's a reply-based, low-friction CTA to a trusting audience)
- **Conversion: 2-5 Concierge signups.** At $99/mo, even 3 signups is ~$3,500+ in annual recurring revenue from one email.
### 7. Source justification
Draws from **Jobber lifecycle trigger: Concierge upsell candidates (13-24 months, not on Concierge)** and the **Concierge Upsell Context** block (the $99/mo inclusions, the "is it worth it at year 1.5 / here's the math" framing, the not-pushy voice). Honors Hard Rule 1 (list is pre-filtered past 12 months; copy references the completed year-1 service).
---
## What I deliberately skipped
- **Cold lead re-engagement (1,000):** high volume but lowest intent, and your recent broadcast opens are at 0.4%. Worth doing, but as a standalone news-angle build next week, not competing for this week's send slots.
- **1-year annual service (17):** operational reminder, low revenue lift, and several have legacy-name systems requiring careful merge handling. Better as a transactional Jobber trigger than a campaign.
- **RO replacement (34):** viable, but the referral and Concierge plays have stronger revenue-per-send this week.
Want me to build out the cold-lead re-engagement with a water-news hook for next week?
